text:
Ottawa's top center is playing like one. Tim Stützle has 28 points in 23 games at almost 22 minutes a night, and the Senators own 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there. He rides a four-game point streak into the weekend.

Some of it will cool. He has 11 goals on 7.3 expected, shooting 20%, and that finishing rate rarely lasts even for a skilled shooter. The flip side: his teammates have scored 3.5 fewer goals than their chances with him on the ice, so the assists have room to catch up while the goals settle.

The engine is the puck in his hands. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying in on 62% of his entries last season and ranked his 10.5 primary shot assists per 60 in the 95th percentile of forwards. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 2.6 wins above replacement, with one real cost: opponents got more chances with him on (bottom 4% of forwards). Watch his own end as closely as his entries.
